units.function: Large mocked route-policy suite for Agent Issue/comment/document/artifact/attachment/approval mutations, Run checkout ownership, attribution anti-spoofing, recovery containment and task-watchdog scoped authority.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest -> monolithic Issue routes -> access/Run/watchdog/recovery/Issue/storage/activity services; services and transactions are mocked, while authorization spans company, Issue, checkout, assignment and special Run scopes.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent actor, scoped API key, Issue assignee/responsible human, heartbeat Run/context snapshot, active checkout, artifact/document/attachment, recovery action, task watchdog, subtree and policy decision.
units.lifecycle: Resolve tenant and actor -> load Issue/Run special scope -> decide read/mutate/assign -> enforce checkout and capability restrictions -> derive attribution -> mutate -> perform best-effort revalidation/wakeup/activity; watchdog paths revalidate current source and serialize recovery fan-out.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed run failed 76/76 only because TCP bind was prohibited; approved unsandboxed run passed 76/76 with expected non-fatal cleanup/revalidation warnings. Policy breadth is excellent, but mocked transactions cannot prove atomicity, races, tenant filtering, idempotency or audit durability.
units.designRationale: Permit collaboration and bounded recovery without letting peer Agents overwrite active work, forge human/Run attribution, escape tenant boundaries, turn cheap recovery into deliverable work or let stale watchdogs fan out mutations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral execution contracts that bind every Agent mutation to capability, Run, Work, tenant, responsible human and evidence while allowing narrowly governed cross-Agent intervention and human collaboration.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the layered tenant/read/mutate/checkout/assignment decisions, 404 existence-oracle defense, server-derived Agent/Run attribution, cheap-recovery capability restrictions, actionable typed denials, watchdog persisted backing/subtree/current-state revalidation and serialized recovery lane. Reimplement behind smaller application policies with transactional authorization/write/evidence, grant provenance/version/expiry, accountable-human approval, idempotency and runtime attestation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Board actors and checkout-management grants bypass active Agent ownership, while watchdogs can change cross-Agent state and assignment without asserted accountable-human authorization. Activity and post-commit revalidation are not atomic evidence; a named operational owner is not the legally accountable human.
evidence: git history: 28 commits from e8ae5286eb92a86ddd7421d1ca22398982a3381d through 7a329fb8bb9f74cdd75f3f7789c43fab0b2e7581 recorded in read ledger
2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 0/76 passed due TCP listen EPERM
2026-08-19 approved unsandboxed focused Vitest: 76/76 passed with expected best-effort warnings
units.securityFindings: HIGH responsibility gap: special grants/watchdogs lack asserted accountable-human issuer, approval and evidence chain. HIGH TOCTOU gap: mocked pass-through transactions do not prove authorization/revalidation/write atomicity. HIGH audit gap: anti-spoof activity is asserted but durable transactional receipts for all mutations are not. HIGH runtime-proof gap: Run context is database/environment identity, not short-lived attestation. MEDIUM revocation/idempotency gap: grant/watchdog revocation races and duplicate requests are absent. MEDIUM broad-route risk: many mutation surfaces share a monolithic orchestration boundary.
